citations.title: Reporting Requirements
citations.requirement: CCL report by the next working day, then a written report within 7 days, for: any death; deaths from injury, abuse or other than natural causes (including deaths away from the facility); AED use; injury needing medical treatment; unusual incident or client absence that threatens health or safety; suspected psychological abuse; epidemic outbreaks; poisonings; catastrophes; fires or explosions. Written report must give client name/age/sex/admission date, date and nature of event, physician findings and treatment, and disposition. (c)-(d): suspected physical abuse of a dependent adult goes to the local ombudsman, CCL and law enforcement within 2 hours if serious bodily injury, otherwise within 24 hours (WIC 15630(b)(1)). (e): within 10 working days report organizational changes, mailing address changes, change of corporate CEO (with fingerprints), and plan-of-operation changes that affect services. (f)-(i): items (b)(1)(A)-(H) also go to the authorized representative; (E)-(G) go to the local health officer when appropriate; epidemic outbreaks go immediately to the local fire authority; substantiated complaints are copied to designated parties.

citations.title: Personal Rights
citations.requirement: (a)(1)-(10) personal rights: dignity; safe and comfortable accommodations; freedom from corporal or unusual punishment, humiliation, intimidation, ridicule, coercion, threat, mental abuse, punitive actions, interference with eating/sleeping/toileting, and withholding of shelter, clothing, medication or aids; being told the CCL complaint unit address and phone and confidentiality information; religious freedom; leaving the facility at any time (curfews and house rules allowed; not applicable to clients with a conservator or other legal authority); not being locked in any room or the premises (exterior doors and windows may be locked if clients can exit; other securing means need prior CCL approval); no restraining devices (postural supports and protective devices only under strict conditions); right to receive or reject medical care; being told the visiting policy (HSC 1512). (d) at admission the client and authorized representative are personally advised of and given the list of rights; (e) rights and visiting policy are posted prominently; (f) the licensee ensures the rights are honored.

citations.title: Health-Related Services
citations.requirement: Licensee ensures first aid and needed medical/dental care, including transportation. Clients are assisted with self-administration of prescription and nonprescription medications. ARF staff may assist with metered-dose and dry-powder inhalers only after training by a licensed professional, with written documentation of procedures and trained staff names, annual review by the professional, and training documented in personnel files. Staff may not give injections except as authorized by law; designated staff may assist with self-administration of injections. No forcing, hiding or camouflaging medication. PRN rules in (b)(4)-(6). Oxygen requirements in (e). First-aid training for direct care staff (f). First-aid supplies list (g). Emergency communication person and contact list at all times (h). Central storage rules (j)-(k) with records kept at least 1 year. Destruction of unretained prescriptions witnessed by the administrator and one other adult non-client, record kept at least 1 year (l).

citations.title: Personnel Requirements (general)
citations.requirement: Personnel competent and in numbers needed to meet client needs; CCL may require added staff (documented, with written reasons), considering client needs, services, physical plant and any emergency or disaster. Volunteers must be supervised and are not counted in the staffing plan. Staff who supervise or give care must be 18+. Direct supervision at potentially dangerous activities or areas; an adult non-client present whenever clients use a pool or body of water needing swim rescue, with a valid water safety certificate. On-the-job training topics in (f). Health screening including TB test by or under a physician no more than 1 year before or 7 days after employment (g). Ill personnel relieved of duty (h). California criminal record clearance or exemption before employment or initial presence (i). Clients are not substitutes for required staff (j). Coverage by capable personnel during absences (k). Care without physical or verbal abuse, exploitation or prejudice (l). All personnel instructed to report personal-rights violations (m). (o): ARFs using secured perimeters must train direct care staff in Emergency Intervention (§85300).

citations.title: ARF Application for License
citations.requirement: Financial plan of operation on CDSS forms. Start-up funds must cover the first three months of operation, and CCL may require written verification. Applicant submits administrator name, addresses, background and qualifications, and documentation of required education and administrator certification.

citations.title: ARF Personnel Requirements
citations.requirement: Licensee employs staff as necessary to provide care and supervision that meets client needs (b), and support staff for office work, cooking, cleaning, laundry and maintenance (c). Food service staffing must ensure clients' food service needs are met (e)(1). Services requiring specialized skills must be performed by licensed or certified personnel; where no license or certification exists, prior CCL approval is required for an unlicensed person to provide the service (f).

citations.title: Night Supervision
citations.requirement: Night staff (10 p.m.-7 a.m.) must be able to help in an emergency and be trained in the facility's planned emergency procedures and in first aid (b). Facilities with 15 or fewer clients need at least one person on call on the premises (c). For 7+ clients who rely on others for all ADLs, one person on duty, on the premises and awake, plus one more per additional 14 such clients (f). For Regional Center clients who rely on others for all ADLs, night supervision is as the RC requires but no less than (f)/(f)(1) (g). Where a signal system is required (§85088), a staff person is responsible for responding to it (i).

citations.title: Needs and Services Plan
citations.requirement: Before admission the licensee determines the program can meet the person's needs, then completes a written Needs and Services Plan. The plan covers: client desires and background; entrance to the facility; specific service needs; written medical assessment (§80069); mental and emotional functioning; mental health intake assessment if any (§85069.3); functional capabilities assessment (§80069.2); the HSC 1180.4(a) initial assessment on or before the day of admission; the individual emergency intervention plan (§85168.2(a)); and facility plans to meet the needs. The 1180.4(a) assessment includes input from the client, authorized representative and any person the client chooses; the client's advance directive on de-escalation, seclusion or manual restraint (honored unless it violates law or endangers safety); early warning signs and triggers; calming techniques; medical conditions raising restraint risk; and trauma history. If the client has a restricted health condition (§80092), the plan includes the Restricted Health Condition Care Plan (§80092.2). Involve the client or representative, participating relatives, the placement or referral agency, and the person responsible for admissions.

citations.title: Consumer Notes, Quarterly and Semi-Annual Reports
citations.requirement: Text fetched is the version operative until 5/1/2026: administrator ensures ongoing written consumer notes (community and leisure activities, overnight visits away, illness, SIRs, medical and dental visits, dated and signed entries); semi-annual progress reports for Service Level 2 and 3 facilities; quarterly reports for Level 4 (data summary under §56013(d)(4), barriers and actions taken) sent to the service coordinator within 30 days of quarter end. A version operative 5/1/2026 (amended in the DDS SIR rulemaking) is listed in LII but its text was NOT fetched. Confirm current text and how it applies to Levels 5-6.

citations.title: Personal Rights (ARF)
citations.requirement: Adds to §80072. Section number and title confirmed in the LII Article 6 index; full text not fetched. Subsections seen in search excerpts (LII, CDSS ARF self-assessment): (b)(1) visit before admission; (b)(2) relatives and authorized representative informed of care activities, including NSP changes; (b)(3) prompt answers to relatives' communications; (b)(4) private visits including advocacy representatives during waking hours; (b)(5) own clothes; (b)(6) personal items; (b)(7) possess and control own cash; (b)(8) individual storage; (b)(9) confidential phone calls; (b)(10) unopened mail; (b)(11) help voting; (b)(12) move from the facility per the admission agreement. Confirm against full text.

citations.title: Day Staff-Client Ratio
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: for Regional Center clients who rely on others for all ADLs, day staffing is as the RC specifies, no less than 1:3.

citations.title: ARF Buildings and Grounds
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: no more than two clients per bedroom; bedrooms not used as passageways.

citations.title: Fixtures, Furniture, Equipment and Supplies
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: 1 toilet and washbasin per 6 persons and 1 tub or shower per 10, counting live-in staff and family; per-resident bed, chair, nightstand, lamp and drawers (2 drawers or 8 cu ft); linens; hygiene supplies; emergency lighting; night lights; signal system where required.

citations.title: Fire Clearance
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: fire clearance is obtained through CCL; a separate clearance is required before admitting nonambulatory clients or persons 65+. §80072(a)(8)(D) requires a fire clearance before using a postural support that makes a client nonambulatory.

citations.title: Criminal Record Clearance
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: Live Scan clearance or exemption is required before staff presence. §80065(i) confirms clearance, exemption or an approved transfer before employment or initial presence; §80019(d) fingerprints are required for a new corporate CEO.

citations.title: Plan of Operation
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: written plan covering purpose, admissions, admission agreement, staffing plan, in-service plan, floor plan and grounds sketch, menus, transportation, rate and refund policy, handling of resident money, consultants and visiting policy. It must be kept current; changes that affect services go to CCL within 10 working days (§80061(e)(4)).

citations.title: ARF Plan of Operation
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research checklist: ARF plan of operation includes the infection control plan (§85022(a)(1)) and consultants (§85022(a)(2)).

citations.title: Application for License
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: CCL orientation is completed before filing; sets application contents, including the lease and landlord information in (d)(3).

citations.title: ARF Administrator Qualifications and Duties
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: certified administrator, age 21+, high school diploma or GED; HIV/TB training within six months of becoming administrator and updated every two years ((k)); 7-15 client homes need one year of residential care experience.

citations.title: ARF Administrator Certification Requirements
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: 35-hour CDSS-approved Initial Certification Training Program; exam within 60 days of finishing, maximum 3 attempts ($100); apply on LIC 9214 within 30 days of passing, with LIC 508 and Live Scan (LIC 9163), $140 fee.

citations.title: ARF Administrator Recertification Requirements
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: 40 hours of continuing education every two years (4 hours on laws and regulations); up to 24 hours of RC-approved DDS training may count.

citations.title: Facility Service Levels
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: basic direct care staffing whenever residents are under facility supervision: Level 2 1 per up to 6; Levels 3/4A/4B 1 per up to 3; 4C-4E 1 per up to 2; 4F-4I 1 for the first resident. Above those resident counts, weekly direct care hours are added by level (§56004(d) table); 2-7 hours per resident per week of program preparation can count. Consultant hours of 8/12/16 per consumer per six months (§56004(f)). The text uses legacy levels; map to Levels 2-6 using the DDS crosswalk (L3 = old 3/4A/4B; L4 = 4C-4E; L5 = 4F-4H; L6 = 4I).

citations.title: Facility Service Level Approval Process
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: written service level request with administrator qualifications; RC decides within 45 days; a level change is allowed only on a change of ownership or when most residents' ID teams identify a new need ((c)(1)).

citations.title: Residential Services Orientation
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: the administrator completes the RC residential services orientation before the first admission. RCs hold it at least every six months.

citations.title: Program Design Requirements
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: written program design with org chart, purpose and outcomes, entrance/exit criteria, program preparation duties, staff qualifications and duty statements, sample schedule and training plan; Level 3 and 4 designs have extra content.

citations.title: Direct Care Staff Competency-Based Training and Testing
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: two 35-hour DSPT segments (year 1 and year 2) with tests or a challenge test; §56033(a)(2)(B) segment 2 within two years of hire. DDS DSPT is free to first- and second-year DSPs (dds.ca.gov/services/dspt).

citations.title: Administrator Qualifications and Continuing Education
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: 6/9/12 months of DD experience for Level 2/3/4 (RC may waive); 8/12/12 hours of annual continuing education.

citations.title: Direct Care Staff Qualifications and Continuing Education
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: 40-hour on-site orientation ((a)(1)) covering program design, IPPs, rights, medications, emergencies and fire, SIRs and abuse reporting; CE of 8 hours/year (L2) or 12 hours/year (L3-L4); Level 4 staff without 6 months' experience add 12 hours in the first six months. This section was amended in the DDS SIR rulemaking effective 5/1/2026; confirm current text.

citations.title: Vendor Application Requirements
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: DS 1890 with disclosures, service type (915/905), capacity and consultants; copy of license or proof of application; signed HCBS Provider Agreement ((a)(10)(J)) for Medi-Cal-eligible services.

citations.title: Regional Center Review of Vendor Application
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: 45-day review; the RC cannot approve or refer until the license is received ((c)).

citations.title: General Requirements for Vendors and Regional Centers
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: vendor allows monitoring access ((a)(2)); keeps records at least 5 years ((a)(3)); bills only authorized, delivered services and the rate is payment in full ((a)(10),(12)); vendored by the RC where the facility is located ((a)(14)); HCBS Provider Agreement ((a)(16)); no payment for pre-vendorization services and no referrals before vendorization ((d)(4)).

citations.title: Types of Services
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: service codes 905/910 owner-operated and 915/920 staff-operated residential facilities.

citations.title: Requirements for Special Incident Reporting by Vendors and Long-Term Health Care Facilities
citations.requirement: Not fetched. The LII page seen in search is the version operative until 5/1/2026; the DDS SIR rulemaking effective 5/1/2026 amended 54327, 54327.1, 56002, 56026, 56038, 56059 and 56093. Pre-5/1/2026 text: vendors report to the RC with case management responsibility (and the vendoring RC if different) by phone, email or fax immediately and within 24 hours of learning of the incident, then a written report within 48 hours, and concurrently copy any later written report sent to CCL. Categories include missing consumer with a missing-persons report filed, reasonably suspected abuse (physical, sexual, fiduciary, emotional/mental, physical or chemical restraint) and neglect, and the death of any consumer. DDS FAQ dated 6/12/2026 confirms 24-hour and 48-hour timelines under the amended rule; RCs may add reporting requirements beyond Title 17. Verify the post-5/1/2026 category list before finalizing.

citations.title: Special Incidents
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the LII Title 17 Subchapter 4 Article 5 index; text not fetched. Review for residential-facility SIR duties.

citations.title: Consumer IPP Objectives
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the LII Article 5 index; text not fetched. Governs facility handling of consumer IPP objectives.

citations.title: Elder/Dependent Adult Abuse Mandated Reporting
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: mandated reporter duties for abuse of elders and dependent adults. CCL timelines are restated in 22 CCR §80061(c)-(d): 2 hours for suspected physical abuse resulting in serious bodily injury, 24 hours otherwise.

citations.title: Independent audit / independent review of vendors
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: independent review if RC payments are $500,000-$1,999,999 a year; independent audit at $2,000,000 or more; due 9 months after fiscal year end.

citations.title: Lanterman Developmental Disabilities Services Act
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: entitlement to services and the statutory basis for regional center services and vendorization.

citations.title: Rights of persons with developmental disabilities
citations.requirement: Not fetched and not in research. Statutory list of rights of persons with developmental disabilities; verify subsections before citing in the manual.

citations.title: Individual Program Plan
citations.requirement: Cited in the fetched text of 22 CCR §80072(a)(8)(F)1. as the source of the Individual Program Plan (IPP). Section content not fetched; verify.

citations.title: Seclusion and behavioral restraints in facilities
citations.requirement: Not fetched. §1180.4(a) is cross-referenced in the fetched text of 22 CCR §85068.2(b)(1)(G) (initial assessment, advance directive on de-escalation, seclusion and restraint). A Westside Regional Center page lists HSC 1180-1180.6 as the seclusion and restraint law. Verify scope for ARFs.

citations.title: Community care facility license fees
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: 4-6 beds $908 with the application and $454 annual; late annual fee adds 50%. Facility is within the Community Care Facilities Act, HSC §1500 et seq.

policies.category: Section A – Forms by Type of Facility
policies.title: Emergency Disaster Plan (LIC 610D) and Relocation Sites
state_specifics: Complete LIC 610D, the ARF Emergency Disaster Plan, and keep it current.
Name two relocation sites away from the facility. Each must be able to hold the full licensed census.
If the applicant does not yet occupy the property, get written authorization for each relocation site from the agency or person in possession.
Night staff (10 p.m.–7 a.m.) must be trained in the facility's planned emergency procedures and first aid.
Report catastrophes, fires and explosions to CCL by the next working day, with a written report within 7 days.

policies.title: Job Descriptions and Duty Statements
state_specifics: Write a job description for each position: administrator, lead/house manager, direct support professional, support staff.
The Title 17 program design must include staff qualifications and duty statements (§56013).
Duty statements state minimum age (18+ for staff who supervise or give care) and required training.
Tasks needing specialized skills go only to licensed or certified personnel (§85065(f)).

policies.title: Personnel Policies
state_specifics: Employ personnel competent and in numbers sufficient to meet client needs. Volunteers must be supervised and do not count toward staffing.
Staff are relieved of duty when ill (§80065(h)).
Clients may never substitute for required staff (§80065(j)).
Paid sick leave of at least 40 hours or 5 days per year (Labor Code §246). Pay at or above the state minimum wage of $16.90 (2026) or the higher local rate.
Policies must prohibit physical or verbal abuse, exploitation and prejudice, and require every employee to report personal-rights violations.

policies.title: In-Service Training Plan for Staff
state_specifics: Include the in-service plan in the plan of operation. Title 17 continuing education (CE) for direct care staff is 8 hrs/yr at Level 2 and 12 hrs/yr at Levels 3–4.
Level 4 staff without 6 months' experience add 12 hours in their first six months. Confirm the current §56038 text, which was amended effective 5/1/2026.
Staff who assist with inhalers need training by a licensed professional, documented in the personnel file and reviewed annually.
Staff giving direct care need first-aid training. Night staff need emergency procedures and first aid.
Keep a training log for each employee and track DSPT segments.

policies.title: Facility Program Description (Plan of Operation and Title 17 Program Design)
state_specifics: Title 22 plan of operation covers purpose, admissions, staffing, in-service plan, floor plan, menus, transportation, rates and refunds, resident money, consultants and visiting policy.

Title 17 program design (§56013) covers org chart, purpose and outcomes, entrance/exit criteria, program preparation, staff duties, sample schedule and training plan. Level 3 and 4 designs have extra content.
State the service code (915 staff-operated or 905 owner-operated) and the requested service level (Levels 2–6).
Report plan changes that affect services to CCL within 10 working days (§80061(e)).
A level change is allowed only on a change of ownership or when most residents' ID teams identify a new need (§56005(c)(1)).

policies.title: Rules of Discipline and Personal Rights
state_specifics: Prohibit corporal or unusual punishment, humiliation, intimidation, ridicule, coercion, threat, mental abuse, punitive actions, and interference with eating, sleeping or toileting.
Never withhold shelter, clothing, medication or aids as discipline.
House rules and curfews are allowed, but residents may leave at any time unless a conservator or other legal authority applies.
Give each resident and authorized representative the rights list at admission, and post the rights and visiting policy prominently (§80072(d)–(e)).
Give the CCL complaint unit address and phone to each resident.

policies.title: Admission Policies, Referral and Transition In
state_specifics: Accept a first placement only with a CCL license, a vendor number and an approved service level. No referrals or payment before vendorization (§54320(c); §54326(d)(4)).
Before admission, decide the program can meet the person's needs and complete the Needs and Services Plan (§85068.2).
Use a written admission agreement. State the rate and refund policy and the visiting policy.
Obtain a separate fire clearance before admitting nonambulatory residents or anyone 65+.
The administrator completes the regional center residential services orientation before the first admission.

policies.title: Sample Menu and Food Service Plan
state_specifics: Include a sample menu in the plan of operation.
Staffing must ensure residents' food service needs are met (§85065(e)(1)).
Accommodate modified diets and individual needs identified in the Needs and Services Plan.
Post or provide menus. Record any substitutions.

policies.title: Control of Property, Personal Funds and Resident Money
state_specifics: Residents may possess and control their own cash and personal items, with individual storage (§85072(b)(5)–(8)). Confirm against the full text.
If the facility handles resident money, keep it separate from operating funds and describe the procedure in the plan of operation (§80022).
SSI/SSP board-and-care is $1,444.07 per month, paid by the resident or representative payee. The resident keeps $182.00 for personal needs.
Keep ledgers with receipts and signatures, and an itemized property inventory.
The rate is payment in full (§54326(a)(12)). Do not charge residents extra for covered services.

policies.title: Neighborhood Complaint Policy (Non-Resident Owner Homes of Six or Fewer)
state_specifics: Applies only to non-resident-owner community care facilities serving six or fewer. Mark it 'not applicable' if the owner lives in the home.
Name a contact person and phone number so neighbors can raise complaints.
Log each complaint with the date, the response and the resolution.
Keep the policy with the plan of operation (LIC 281 item B15).

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
state_specifics: A certified administrator, age 21+ with a high school diploma or GED, is responsible for the facility.
Report organizational changes, address changes and a new corporate CEO (with fingerprints) to CCL within 10 working days (§80061(e)).
Title 17 experience: 6/9/12 months of developmental-disability experience for Level 2/3/4. The regional center may waive it.
Keep an org chart in the program design.

policies.title: Licensure, Vendorization and Provider Agreements
state_specifics: CDSS CAB licensing takes 90–120 days. Application fee is $908 for 4–6 beds, paid with the application. Annual fee is $454, with a +50% late fee.
The financial plan must show start-up funds for the first three months (§85018).
Vendorization uses DS 1890 and the signed HCBS Provider Agreement. Standardized steps: 15 days to screen, 30 days to confirm completeness (30 days to cure), 45 days to approve or deny.
One vendorization per service per location, with the regional center where the home is located (§54326(a)(14)).
Service codes: 915 staff-operated, 905 owner-operated.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: Review the manual at least annually and whenever regulations change.
Track the DDS Special Incident Reporting amendments effective 5/1/2026 (§§54327, 56026, 56038) and update affected policies.
Send plan-of-operation changes that affect services to CCL within 10 working days.
Keep version dates and staff sign-offs.

policies.title: Quality Improvement, Data Review and Mortality Review
state_specifics: Review incidents, SIRs, consumer notes and quarterly progress-report data at least quarterly.
Level 4 quarterly reports include a data summary, barriers and actions taken (§56026). Confirm how this applies to Levels 5–6.
Review every death for cause and lessons learned.
The Quality Incentive Program (QIP) can earn the other 10% of the rate. Eligibility requires HCBS, EVV and audit compliance.

policies.title: Regional Center Billing, Service Documentation and Independent Audit/Review
state_specifics: Bill the regional center monthly, only for authorized, delivered services (§54326(a)(10)).
Keep billing and service records at least 5 years (§54326(a)(3)).
Independent review if regional center payments are $500,000–$1,999,999 a year. Independent audit at $2,000,000 or more. Both are due 9 months after fiscal year end (WIC §4652.5).
Use EVV if applicable to the service.
New vendors are paid 90% of the regional-center portion plus SSI/SSP. QIP can earn the rest.

policies.title: Licensing and Regional Center Monitoring Access
state_specifics: Allow unannounced CCL visits and regional center monitoring access (§54326(a)(2)).
Designate who receives inspectors and who has authority to show records.
Keep the CCL complaint-unit information and the posted rights visible.
Track and correct all deficiencies, and keep copies of substantiated complaints.

policies.title: Individual Rights and HCBS Settings Requirements
state_specifics: Honor all §80072(a) rights: dignity, religious freedom, receiving or rejecting medical care, and leaving the facility.
Private visits, including advocacy representatives, during waking hours.
Confidential phone calls, unopened mail, own clothing, and help with voting (§85072(b)). Confirm against full text.
Residents are free to come and go. Never lock residents in a room or the premises.
Review the rights with residents at admission and when they change.

policies.title: Rights Restrictions and Due Process
state_specifics: Exterior doors and windows may be locked only if residents can exit. Any other securing means need prior CCL approval.
Postural supports and protective devices are allowed only under strict §80072 conditions. A fire clearance is needed first if the support makes a client nonambulatory.
Document any modification of a right in the plan with the assessed need, less-intrusive methods tried, and informed consent.
Notify the authorized representative and the service coordinator of restrictions.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Tell each resident the CCL complaint unit address and phone number at admission.
Residents may complain to CCL, the regional center, the ombudsman and Disability Rights California without retaliation.
Respond promptly to complaints from relatives and authorized representatives (§85072(b)(3)). Confirm against full text.
Log each complaint and its resolution.
Copies of substantiated complaints go to the designated parties (§80061(i)).

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Residents receive unopened mail and may make confidential phone calls (§85072(b)(9)–(10)). Confirm against full text.
Release information only with consent or as the law allows, including to CCL and the regional center.
Keep records locked and limit access to staff with a need to know.
Train all staff on confidentiality at orientation.

policies.title: Informed Consent and Decision-Making Support
state_specifics: Residents have the right to receive or reject medical care (§80072(a)).
The right to leave the facility does not apply where a conservator or other legal authority exists.
Involve the resident and authorized representative in all planning (§85068.2).
Document consent and capacity concerns, and support residents in making their own choices.
Verify WIC §4502 provisions before citing in resident materials.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Communication Access
federal: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act
state_specifics: Care must be given without prejudice (§80065(l)).
Provide interpreters and accessible communication supports at no cost to the resident.
Record communication needs and preferences in the Needs and Services Plan.
Make reasonable accommodations in admission, services and facility access.

policies.title: Person-Centered Planning, the IPP and the Needs and Services Plan
state_specifics: Complete the written Needs and Services Plan before admission (§85068.2).
The plan includes the medical assessment, functional capabilities assessment, mental health intake if any, and individual emergency intervention plan.
Include the HSC §1180.4(a) initial assessment on or before the day of admission, with the resident's advance directive on de-escalation and restraint.
Include the Restricted Health Condition Care Plan if applicable.
Coordinate with the regional center IPP (WIC §4646; §56022 objectives, text not verified) and update the plan as needs change.

policies.title: Implementation of Supports, Consumer Notes and Progress Reports
state_specifics: The administrator ensures ongoing consumer notes covering community and leisure activities, overnight visits away, illness, SIRs, and medical and dental visits. Entries are dated and signed.
Progress reports: semiannual at Levels 2–3, quarterly at Level 4, sent to the service coordinator within 30 days of quarter end.
The §56026 amendments (effective 5/1/2026) and Levels 5–6 requirements are not verified. Confirm before finalizing.
Count program preparation hours (2–7 per resident per week) toward staffing only as §56004 allows.

policies.title: Community Integration and Employment Choice
state_specifics: Document community and leisure activities in consumer notes.
The program design describes services and outcomes, including community participation.
Support employment and day-program choices identified in the IPP.
Residents may go out and receive visitors (curfews and house rules only as allowed).

policies.title: Transition, Discharge and Termination of Services
state_specifics: Entrance and exit criteria are in the program design (§56013).
Residents may move out per the admission agreement (§85072(b)(12)). Confirm against full text.
State the rate and refund policy in the plan of operation.
Coordinate any discharge with the regional center service coordinator and authorized representative.
Record the transition plan and where belongings and funds went.

policies.title: Assistance with Self-Administered Medications and Staff Training
state_specifics: Staff assist with self-administration only. No injections except as authorized by law. Designated staff may assist with self-administered injections.
Never force, hide or camouflage medication. Follow the PRN rules in §80075(b)(4)–(6).
Inhaler assistance needs training by a licensed professional, documented procedures, annual review and a file record.
Central storage records are kept at least 1 year. Destruction of unretained prescriptions is witnessed by the administrator and one other adult non-client.
Follow the oxygen requirements in §80075(e).

policies.title: Nursing Oversight, Health Care Coordination and Consultants
state_specifics: The licensee ensures needed medical and dental care, including transportation (§80075).
Services needing specialized skills go to licensed or certified personnel. Where no license exists, get prior CCL approval (§85065(f)).
Level 4 requires consultant hours of 8/12/16 per consumer per six months (§56004(f)). List consultants in the plan of operation.
Coordinate with the physician, the regional center and any Restricted Health Condition Care Plan.

policies.title: Health Monitoring, Seizures and Choking Risk
state_specifics: Record each resident's health risks, including seizures, dysphagia and choking, in the Needs and Services Plan.
Direct care staff need first-aid training.
Specialized care goes only to licensed or certified personnel or CCL-approved persons.
Train staff on each resident's individual protocols and document it.
Build the Restricted Health Condition Care Plan if applicable (§80092.2).

policies.title: Change of Condition and Emergency Medical Care
state_specifics: Keep first-aid supplies and an emergency contact list. Have an emergency communication person available at all times (§80075(g)–(h)).
Report injuries needing medical treatment to CCL by the next working day, with a written report within 7 days.
Notify the authorized representative and service coordinator of significant changes.
Update the Needs and Services Plan after a change of condition.
Report poisonings and epidemic outbreaks per §80061.

policies.title: Death of an Individual
state_specifics: Report any death to CCL by the next working day, with a written report within 7 days.
This includes deaths from injury, abuse or other than natural causes, including deaths away from the facility.
Notify the authorized representative and the regional center. Death is an SIR category (confirm the post-5/1/2026 §54327 text).
Written report gives client name, age, sex, admission date, date and nature of event, physician findings and disposition.
Preserve records and complete a mortality review.

policies.title: Positive Behavior Support
state_specifics: Support plans focus on early warning signs, triggers and calming techniques recorded in the Needs and Services Plan.
Use consultants (Level 4: 8/12/16 hours per consumer per six months) for behavioral supports.
No punishment, humiliation or coercion (§80072).
Train staff on each resident's plan and track results in consumer notes.

policies.title: Restrictive Interventions, Restraint and Seclusion
state_specifics: No restraining devices. Postural supports and protective devices only under strict §80072 conditions.
Honor the resident's advance directive on de-escalation, seclusion and manual restraint unless it violates law or endangers safety.
Facilities with secured perimeters must train direct care staff in Emergency Intervention (§85300) (§80065(o)).
The individual emergency intervention plan is part of the Needs and Services Plan.
Verify the scope of HSC §1180–1180.6 for ARFs before finalizing.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Staff are mandated reporters of dependent adult abuse (WIC §15630).
Suspected physical abuse with serious bodily injury goes to the ombudsman, CCL and law enforcement within 2 hours. Otherwise within 24 hours.
Report suspected psychological abuse to CCL by the next working day, with a written report within 7 days.
Report to the regional center as an SIR (§54327).
All personnel must report personal-rights violations (§80065(m)). No retaliation.

policies.title: Reportable Incidents, Special Incident Reports and Investigations
state_specifics: CCL: report by the next working day, with a written report within 7 days (§80061).
Regional center SIR: pre-5/1/2026 text was by phone/email/fax immediately and within 24 hours, then written within 48 hours. DDS confirms 24/48-hour timelines under the amended rule.
Copy the regional center on any later written report sent to CCL.
Record SIRs in consumer notes.
Verify the post-5/1/2026 category list in §54327 and §56027 before finalizing.

policies.title: Missing Person and Elopement
state_specifics: Residents may leave at any time, so elopement protocols apply only to clients at risk. Do not use locks to prevent exit without CCL approval.
Report a client absence that threatens health or safety to CCL by the next working day, with a written report within 7 days.
A missing consumer with a missing-persons report filed is an SIR category.
Document individual risk and response in the Needs and Services Plan.

policies.title: Residential Environment, Accessibility and Bedrooms
state_specifics: No more than two clients per bedroom. Bedrooms may not be passageways.
One toilet and washbasin per 6 persons and one tub or shower per 10, counting live-in staff and family.
Per resident: bed, chair, nightstand, lamp, and drawers (2 drawers or 8 cu ft). Provide linens, hygiene supplies, emergency lighting and night lights.
Separate fire clearance before admitting nonambulatory clients or persons 65+.
The lease must allow licensed residential care (§80018(d)(3)).

policies.title: Fire Safety, Emergency Preparedness and Drills
state_specifics: Obtain fire clearance through CCL. Nonambulatory residents need a separate clearance.
Staff must know emergency procedures. Night staff are trained in them and first aid.
Where a signal system is required, a staff person must respond to it (§85065.6(i)).
Report fires and explosions to CCL by the next working day, with a written report within 7 days.
Verify the fire drill frequency and recordkeeping rule in Title 22 before finalizing.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Keep the LIC 9282 infection control plan with the plan of operation (§85022(a)(1)).
Report epidemic outbreaks to CCL by the next working day, with a written report within 7 days. Notify the local fire authority immediately and the local health officer when appropriate.
Staff health screening and TB test no more than 1 year before or 7 days after employment.
Relieve ill personnel of duty.

policies.title: Food, Nutrition and Modified Diets
state_specifics: Staffing must ensure residents' food service needs are met (§85065(e)(1)).
Record modified diets and food allergies in the Needs and Services Plan.
Keep menus current and follow the plan of operation.
Document dysphagia or choking precautions and train staff.

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
state_specifics: The plan of operation describes transportation.
The licensee ensures transportation to medical and dental care (§80075).
Keep valid driver licenses in personnel files for staff who drive.
Direct supervision at potentially dangerous activities (§80065).

policies.title: Water Safety (Pools and Bodies of Water, If Applicable)
state_specifics: Whenever residents use a pool or body of water needing swim rescue, an adult non-client with a valid water safety certificate must be present (§80065).
Applies only if the home has or uses a pool or similar water.
Supervise water activity directly.
Record each resident's swimming ability in the Needs and Services Plan.

policies.title: Staffing Ratios, Supervision and Awake Overnight Staff
state_specifics: Title 17 minimums: Level 2, 1 direct care staff per 6 residents; Level 3, 1 per 3; Level 4, 1 per 2; Levels 5–6, 1 for the first resident. Homes above those counts add weekly direct care hours by level (§56004(d)).
Day staffing for regional center clients who rely on others for all ADLs is as the RC specifies, no less than 1:3 (§85065.5).
Night (10 p.m.–7 a.m.): homes of 15 or fewer need one person on call on the premises. For RC clients needing total care, staffing is as the RC requires (§85065.6).
DDS rate models for Level 3 and above assume awake staff around the clock.
CCL may require added staff. Volunteers and clients do not count toward ratios.

policies.title: Criminal Record Clearance (Live Scan) and Exemptions
state_specifics: Staff need a California criminal record clearance, exemption or approved transfer before employment or initial presence.
Fingerprints are required for a new corporate CEO (§80019(d)).
The administrator applies with Live Scan (LIC 9163) and LIC 508.
No staff work or are present without clearance.
The research does not cover separate registry checks, so confirm any additional requirement with CCL and the regional center.

policies.title: Direct Support Professional Orientation and Training
state_specifics: 40-hour on-site orientation for new direct care staff (§56038(a)(1)): program design, IPPs, rights, medications, emergencies and fire, SIRs, and abuse reporting.
DSPT: two 35-hour competency-based segments (year 1 and year 2), with tests or a challenge test. DSPT is free to the DSP.
Segment 2 is due within two years of hire (§56033(a)(2)(B)).
Night staff must have emergency procedures and first-aid training.
Pay staff for required training time.

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: Health screening including a TB test by or under a physician no more than 1 year before or 7 days after employment (§80065(g)).
Relieve ill personnel of duty (§80065(h)).
The administrator completes HIV/TB training within six months of becoming administrator and updates it every two years (§85064(k)).
Keep records in the personnel file.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Keep a file per employee: name, driver's license if driving, start date, age statement, training records, health screening, TB test and criminal record clearance or exemption.
Document inhaler training in the personnel file (§80075).
Record DSPT, orientation and CE hours.
Keep records available for CCL and regional center review.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Care is provided without physical or verbal abuse, exploitation or prejudice (§80065(l)).
Staff may not borrow from or take property or money of residents, or use residents as substitutes for staff.
All staff must report personal-rights violations (§80065(m)).
Respect residents' privacy and dignity (§80072).

policies.title: Administrator Certification, Qualifications and Continuing Education
state_specifics: 35-hour ICTP, then exam within 60 days (max 3 attempts, $100). Apply on LIC 9214 within 30 days of passing, with LIC 508 and Live Scan; $140 fee.
Recertify every two years with 40 hours of CE, 4 of them on laws and regulations. Up to 24 hours of RC-approved DDS training may count.
Title 17 administrator CE is 8/12/12 hours a year by level (§56037).
HIV/TB training within six months of becoming administrator; update every two years.
Complete the regional center residential orientation before the first admission.

policies.title: Wage and Hour and Labor Compliance
state_specifics: California minimum wage is $16.90 (2026). Higher local rates apply, e.g., City of LA $18.42 and San Diego $17.75.
The DDS rate-model DSP wage of $18.20 may be below some local minimums.
Paid sick leave: at least 40 hours or 5 days a year (Labor Code §246).
24-hour shifts, sleep time and meal/rest rules need employment counsel (Wage Order 5; not verified here).

policies.title: Individual Records and Retention
state_specifics: Keep the Needs and Services Plan, assessments, consumer notes and progress reports in each resident's record.
Vendor billing and service records are kept at least 5 years (§54326(a)(3)).
Medication storage and destruction records are kept at least 1 year (§80075).
Keep records locked, with access limited and logged.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State and Regional Center
state_specifics: CCL: next-working-day report plus written report within 7 days for the events in §80061(b).
Change reports to CCL within 10 working days (§80061(e)).
Regional center SIRs under §54327 (amended 5/1/2026) and consumer progress reports under §56026.
Independent review or audit reports are due 9 months after fiscal year end (WIC §4652.5).
Annual CCL fee of $454 for 4–6 beds, with a +50% late fee.

documents.title: Application Instructions for a Facility License (Application Booklet for Facility License), Sections A and B; covers Adult Residential Facilities
documents.issuer: California Department of Social Services, Community Care Licensing Division
documents.version: LIC 281 (9/04), as supplied by the owner. I could not check ccld.ca.gov or cdss.ca.gov for a newer version (no tools available), so the 9/04 edition is used and should be confirmed with the Centralized Applications Bureau. The supplied text ends partway through item B1, so the narrative instructions for B2–B18 were not available. Items below come from the Section A and Section B tables.
documents.how_used: Section B is the plan-of-operation and supportive-documents checklist for ARF applicants. Only policy and program-content items that the table marks Required for the Adult Residential Facility column are listed. Application forms, financial documents, ownership documents, certificates, the sketch, the fire inspection and the water analysis are excluded. A14 (Emergency Disaster Plan, LIC 610D for ARF) is included as a plan item.

required_items.text: Emergency Disaster Plan (LIC 610D for Adult Residential Facilities). The plan must show two relocation sites away from the facility that are able to accommodate the number of clients in the facility. If the applicant does not currently occupy the property, use of a relocation site requires authorization from the agency or person in possession, verified in writing.
Neighborhood Complaint Policy – Applicable to non-resident owner community care facilities providing residential care for six or fewer persons ONLY.

sections: Section A – Forms by Type of Facility (only A14 Emergency Disaster Plan is policy content)
Section B – Supportive Documents (B4–B11 and B15 are policy and program items for ARFs)

official.notes: The booklet says the application fee plus Section A and B documents must be submitted to the licensing agency as one packet, in the same sequence as the booklet. Incomplete packets are returned in full. Originals must carry original signatures, and the applicant should keep a photocopy. Excluded Section A items: LIC 200, 215, 308, 309, 400, 402, 401, 401a, 403, 403a, 404, 500, 501, 503, 508, 999 and 9054. Excluded Section B items: B1 (partnership/corporate documents), B2 (administrator qualification and certification), B12 (water bacteriological analysis), B16 (first aid card) and B17 (orientation certification). Items that do not apply to ARFs: B3 (social worker qualifications; group home and FFA only), B13 and B14 (insurance and theft & loss; RCFE only), B18 (group home and FFA rate-setting statement) and A17. The Section B table columns are merged in the supplied text. B15 is read as applying to the group-home and ARF columns, and it is conditional on a non-resident owner and a facility of six or fewer. A14 uses LIC 610D for ARFs per the table. The supplied text does not give the content criteria for B4–B11 and B15, so they are listed by title only. For the detailed required content of the plan of operation, use the Title 22 ARF regulations (22 CCR §85000 et seq. and §80000 et seq.). Title 17 vendorization documents required by the regional center are separate and were not in the supplied document.
